rule.title: Explicit Definition of Bounded Contexts
rule.statement: Each subsystem must maintain an explicit Bounded Context with its own Ubiquitous Language; domain models must not be shared indiscriminately across contexts.
rule.rationale: Sharing a single entity class across ingestion, billing, vector indexing, and chat results in an bloated entity with conflicting invariants.
rule.implementation_guidance: Define separate models for IngestionDocument (file buffer, extraction metadata) and RagDocument (vector embeddings, chunks, citations).

forbidden.example: A single giant Document class with 50 optional properties catering to every subsystem.

preferred.example: Separate DocumentIngestionEntity and RagVectorEntity with explicit boundary mapper.

source.evidence_quote: A bounded context is a boundary within a domain where a particular domain model applies... dividing a system into bounded contexts protects against model pollution.

rule.title: Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) for External Services
rule.statement: Third-party APIs (e.g. Gemini, DeepSeek, S3) must be isolated behind an Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) that translates vendor payloads into internal domain models.
rule.rationale: Directly exposing external schemas in application code tightly couples the codebase to third-party vendor contracts, making provider switching or SDK upgrades painful.
rule.implementation_guidance: Wrap external clients in adapter classes (e.g., GeminiEmbeddingAdapter) implementing an internal interface (IEmbeddingService).

forbidden.example: Passing GoogleGenAI.GenerateContentResponse directly through controllers and services.

source.evidence_quote: An anti-corruption layer translates between two bounded contexts or an external system, preventing foreign concepts and models from polluting the internal model.
